description: This course examines how organisations design and improve adaptive decision systems under uncertainty. It begins with A/B testing and experimental design as foundations for evaluating interventions, before progressing to multi-armed bandits, contextual bandits and Bayesian approaches to sequential decision-making. Students will learn how adaptive methods balance exploration and exploitation, incorporate contextual information, and optimise decisions when feedback is partial or evolving. Applications include AI agent design, recommender systems, online marketing, pricing, healthcare decision-making and personalised digital services. Through these topics, the course connects causal evaluation with algorithmic optimisation and prepares students to design analytics-driven systems that learn and adapt over time.
